Some include it under the heading of concision (ījāz), since it branches off from it, but Qudāma made it a branch of the harmony of wording with meaning. Its explanation is that a small amount of wording indicates a great deal of meaning, so that the indication of the wording to the meaning is like pointing with the hand: with a single movement it points to many things which, if expressed by their names, would need a long expression and many words.
So the words of Allah the Exalted «فَانْبِذْ إِلَيْهِمْ عَلى سَواءٍ» point to the command to fight by casting off the covenant just as they cast off your covenant, together with the justice indicated by the command to act equally [Translator's note: the source reads «سال. مر بالمساواة», evidently garbled for «الأمر بالمساواة»]. If you add to that what the word «خيانة» points to, namely the existence of a previous treaty, it becomes clear to you what meanings these hidden allusions contain, as though they were a spell of magic.

* Benefits:
1- When is the covenant with the disbelievers broken?
This verse makes clear a legal ruling, namely the permissibility of annulling contracts of safe conduct with the disbelievers when we fear their treachery and betrayal, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did with Banū Qurayẓa and al-Naḍīr when their treachery appeared. It is likewise obligatory to inform them of that annulment, so that no blame remains on the Muslims. But if they act treacherously and betray the covenant, informing them is not a condition, as happened with the disbelievers of Mecca when they broke the Truce of al-Ḥudaybiyya: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ marched on them without informing them.
A hadith has come on this matter: From Sulaym ibn ʿĀmir, from a man of Ḥimyar, who said: There was a covenant between Muʿāwiya and the Byzantines, and he was marching towards their lands to draw near, so that when the covenant expired he would raid them. Then a man came on a horse saying: "Allahu akbar, Allahu akbar! Fidelity, not treachery!" — and it was ʿAmr ibn ʿAnbasa. Muʿāwiya sent for him and asked him, and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Whoever has a covenant between himself and a people, let him not tighten a knot nor untie it until its term expires, or let him cast it back to them on equal terms." So Muʿāwiya went back. Narrated by Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī.
2- (The redundant) «ما»: In this verse occur the words of Allah the Exalted «وَإِمَّا تَخافَنَّ مِنْ قَوْمٍ خِيانَةً فَانْبِذْ إِلَيْهِمْ عَلى سَواءٍ». We are concerned here with (إما), which is composed of the conditional «إن» and the redundant «ما». The grammarians said: in this case it is permissible to emphasise the verb or not to emphasise it, but the style of the Noble Qur'an has consistently emphasised it. The redundant «ما» occurs in many positions, of which we shall mention the most important:
1- After «إذا», as in the poet's words:
إذا ما الملك سام الناس خسفا ... أبينا أن نقر الذل فينا
(When a king inflicts humiliation on the people, we refuse to let abasement settle among us.)
2- After some prepositions, such as the bāʾ, as in the words of Allah the Exalted «فَبِما رَحْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ لِنْتَ لَهُمْ».
And after «عن», as in the words of Allah the Exalted «عَمَّا قَلِيلٍ لَيُصْبِحُنَّ نادِمِينَ».
3- It is added between the followed word and its follower, as in the words of Allah the Exalted «مَثَلًا ما بَعُوضَةً». Al-Zajjāj said: «ما» is a particle added for emphasis according to all the Basrans, and «بعوضة» is a badal (substitute).
4- It is added after «سيّ», as in the words of Imruʾ al-Qays:
ألا رب يوم لك منهن صالح ... ولا سيما يوم بدارة جلجل
(How many a good day you have had with them — and especially a day at Dārat Juljul.)

safi-cedvel:59-59.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لا) of prohibition, governing the jussive; (تحسبنّ) imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the jussive, and (النون) is for emphasis; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent) [Note: Al-ʿUkbarī permitted making the fāʿil implied, i.e. (من خلفهم) "whoever is behind them" or (أحد) "anyone", so that the relative noun becomes the first mafʿūl bihi.], and the first object is omitted, its implied form being "themselves"; (كفروا) past verb and its fāʿil; (سبقوا) like «كفروا»; (إنّ) a particle of emphasis governing the accusative, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna; (لا) negating; (يعجزون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) …
and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «لا تحسبنّ الذين …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «كفروا …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «إنّهم لا يعجزون» has no grammatical position, giving the reason (taʿlīliyya) — or an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) —. The clause «لا يعجزون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna.

safi-cedvel:7-8.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (إذ) an adverbial noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكروا (remember); (يعد) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative; (إحدى) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (الطائفتين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb – an abrogator (nāsikh) – and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as ism of anna; (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of anna.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّها لكم) is in the position of the accusative as badal (substitute) of the second object إحدى.. i.e. He promises you possession of one of the two parties. (الواو) conjunctive – or circumstantial (ḥāliyya) –; (تودّون) imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (أن) like the first; (غير) ism of anna, accusative; (ذات) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الشوكة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (تكون) a complete imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «it» (هي), i.e. غير ذات الشوكة; (لكم) like the first, attached to (تكون).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ غير ذات ...) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being تودّون.
(الواو) conjunctive; (يريد) imperfect verb, nominative; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle of the accusative; (يحقّ) imperfect verb, accusative, and the fāʿil is «he»; (الحقّ) mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يحقّ) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, its governor being يريد.
(بكلمات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يحقّ), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunctive; (يقطع دابر) like يحقّ الحقّ and conjoined to it; (الكافرين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «(اذكروا) إذ يعدكم» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يعدكم ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تودّون ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause يعدكم [Note: Or in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object pronoun in (يعدكم).].
The clause «تكون لكم» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of anna.
The clause «يريد الله» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يحقّ الحقّ» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «يقطع ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يحقّ.
(اللام) the lām of causation (taʿlīl); (يحقّ) imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, and the fāʿil is «he», i.e. Allah; (الحقّ) like the first; (الواو) conjunctive; (يبطل الباطل) like يحقّ الحقّ and conjoined to it; (الواو) circumstantial; (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle; (كره) past verb; (المجرمون) fāʿil, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يحقّ ...) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being «He commanded you to fight» (أمركم بالقتال).
The clause «يحقّ ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يبطل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يحقّ ...
The clause «كره المجرمون» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl of the object of the command, the linking pronoun being implied, i.e. even if the criminals dislike that.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the content of the preceding speech, i.e.: even if the criminals dislike the fighting, Allah has commanded you to it in order to establish the truth.

* Morphology:
(الشوكة): a noun meaning strength and might; its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa on the fāʾ, and it is borrowed from the singular of الشوك (thorns).

* Rhetoric:
The general and the specific (al-ʿumūm wa-l-khuṣūṣ): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «لِيُحِقَّ الْحَقَّ وَيُبْطِلَ الْباطِلَ» after His saying «يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُحِقَّ الْحَقَّ بِكَلِماتِهِ». The verification in distinguishing the two statements is that in the first the will is mentioned absolutely, not restricted to the particular event, as though it were said: you would like the unarmed party to be yours, while it is Allah the Exalted's way to will the establishing of the truth and the effacing of disbelief absolutely; and because of His will to establish the truth and abolish falsehood He assigned to you the armed party. So between the two statements there is generality and specificity, absoluteness and restriction. And in that there is evident intensification in emphasising the meaning by mentioning it in two ways: absolute and restricted.

safi-cedvel:9-9.t:
* I'rab:
(إذ) badal (substitute) of (إذ يعدكم), in the position of the accusative [Note: Or attached to the verb تودّون.], (تستغيثون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (ربّ) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الفاء) conjunctive; (استجاب) past verb, and the fāʿil is «he»; (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (استجاب), (أنّي) a particle resembling the verb and its ism; (ممدّ) khabar (predicate), nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (بألف) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the active participle ممدّ; (من الملائكة) a preposition and its genitive noun, naʿt (adjective) of ألف; (مردفين) ḥāl (circumstantial) of ألف, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّي ممدّكم) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, its implied form being بأنّي ممدّكم, attached to (استجاب).
The clause «تستغيثون ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «استجاب» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause تستغيثون.

* Morphology:
(استجاب): the alif is changed from a wāw; its origin is استجوب. The wāw came vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was changed into «the fāʾ» [Translator's note: so in the source; «into an alif» is evidently meant.]; its pattern is استفعل [Note: The alif, sīn and tāʾ in the verb are extra without indicating anything, in contrast to تستغيثون, where they are extra for seeking.].
(ممدّكم): the active participle of the quadriliteral أمدّ; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn; the kasra of the ʿayn was moved to the letter before it because of the doubling.
(مردفين): plural of مردف, the active participle of the quadriliteral أردف; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Benefits:
1- إذ: an adverb for past time. What can be drawn from its discussion has passed with us, so return to it in its places.
2- From history:
Muḥammad ﷺ called the Muslims to intercept the caravan of Quraysh returning from Syria. Abū Jahl learned of that, so he summoned Quraysh to protect it, and they set out for that. Abū Sufyān was at the head of the caravan; he veered with it onto the coastal road and escaped with it. Abū Jahl learned of that, but he was obstinate and refused anything but to reach the water of Badr, slaughter camels and drink wine.
When the setting-out of Quraysh reached Muḥammad, he consulted his Companions, both Muhājirūn and Anṣār, and opinion settled on meeting the army of the polytheists.
So Muḥammad ﷺ rejoiced and said: Go forth with the blessing of Allah, for Allah has promised me one of the two parties; by Allah, it is as if I am now looking at the places where the people will fall. Then came the battle of Badr, and Allah defeated the polytheists. The Muslims killed seventy of them and took seventy captive. The account of Badr is long; we have contented ourselves with this snippet of it.

safi-cedvel:10-10.t:
* [Note: See the i'rab of this verse also in Sūrat (Āl ʿImrān), verse (126).]
I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) a negative particle; (جعل) past verb, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (بشرى) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) [Note: Or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), the verb being transitive to one object.], the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (الواو) conjunctive; (اللام) for causation (taʿlīl); (تطمئنّ) imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تطمئنّ), (قلوب) fāʿil, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تطمئنّ) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being «He prepared», «He did» or «He made easy» [Note: It may be conjoined to (بشرى) – as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi – and it was put in the genitive by the lām because a condition for the accusative was lacking.].
(الواو) resumptive; (ما) negative, inoperative (muhmala); (النصر) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (إلّا) like the first; (من عند) a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb – an abrogator (nāsikh) –; (الله) the Name of Majesty, ism of inna, accusative; (عزيز) khabar of inna, nominative; (حكيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «جعله الله ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تطمئنّ به قلوبكم» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أنّ) [Translator's note: so written in the source, with a shadda; the implied particle is أن.].
The clause «ما النصر إلا من عند الله» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّ الله عزيز ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).

safi-cedvel:11-11.t:
* I'rab:
(إذ يغشّيكم) like إذ يعدكم [Note: In verse (7) of this sūra.], and the fāʿil (agent) is «he», i.e. Allah; (النعاس) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (أمنة) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the fāʿil [Note: Or of the first object, i.e. possessors of security, with a muḍāf omitted.. And it may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).], (من) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أمنة; (الواو) conjunctive; (ينزّل) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil is «he»; (على) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (ينزّل), (من السماء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ينزّل), (ماء) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (ليطهّر) like لتطمئنّ [Note: In the previous verse (1). [Translator's note: so in the source; the previous verse is (10).], and the fāʿil is «he», and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (به) like منه, attached to (يطهّركم).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يطهّركم) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (ينزّل).
(الواو) conjunctive; (يذهب) like يطهّر and conjoined to it; (عنكم) like عليكم, attached to (يذهب), (رجز) mafʿūl bihi; (الشيطان) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunctive; (ليربط) like ليطهّر; (على قلوب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يربط), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يربط) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (يغشّيكم or ينزل).
(الواو) conjunctive; (يثبّت) imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to (يربط), and the fāʿil is «he»; (به) like منه, attached to (يثبّت), (الأقدام) mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «يغشّيكم ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «ينزّل ...» is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to the clause يغشيكم.
The clause «يطهّركم» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the implied particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «يذهب ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause of the particle-relative.
The clause «يربط ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the second particle-relative (أن).
The clause «يثبّت ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يربط.

safi-cedvel:60-63.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (أعدّوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn … and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أعدّوا); (ما) a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (استطعتم) past verb and its fāʿil; (من قوّة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted referent pronoun; (الواو) conjunction; (من رباط) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what «من قوّة» is attached to; (الخيل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (ترهبون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the retention of the nūn … and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (ترهبون); (عدوّ) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (عدوّكم) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first, accusative … and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (آخرين) conjoined to the first «عدوّ», accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ; (من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, a naʿt (adjective) of «آخرين», and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi; (لا) negating; (تعلمون) like «ترهبون», and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (يعلم) imperfect verb, nominative, and (هم) as before … and the second object of the verb is omitted, its implied form being "alarmed" or "at war"; but the apparent view is that the first verb is transitive to a single object, i.e. "you do not know them"; (الواو) conjunction; (ما) a conditional noun governing the jussive, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi; (تنفقوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn … and the wāw is the fāʿil; (من شيء) tamyīz (specification), accusative, or ḥāl, accusative [Translator's note: so in the source, i.e. in the position of the accusative]; (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb (تنفقوا); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (يوفّ) passive imperfect verb, jussive, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; (إليكم) like «لهم», attached to (يوفّ); (الواو) of the ḥāl; (أنتم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (لا) negating; (تظلمون) passive imperfect verb, nominative … and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil.
The clause «أعدّوا لهم …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «استطعتم» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما), the referent pronoun being omitted, its implied form being «استطعتموه».
The clause «ترهبون به …» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the fāʿil of «أعدّوا» or from its object.
The clause «لا تعلمونهم» is in the position of the accusative as a second naʿt of «آخرين» [Note: Or a naʿt of «عدوّ», «عدوّكم» and «آخرين» together.].
The clause «الله يعلمهم» is in the position of the accusative as a third or further naʿt [Note: It is permissible for it to be an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) with no grammatical position.].
The clause «يعلمهم» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «تنفقوا …» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «يوفّ إليكم» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a jussive condition not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «أنتم لا تظلمون» is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in (إليكم).
The clause «لا تظلمون» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم).
(الواو) conjunction; (إن) a conditional particle governing the jussive; (جنحوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of the jussive as the protasis … and the wāw is the fāʿil; (للسلم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (جنحوا); (الفاء) linking the apodosis of the condition; (اجنح) imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "anta"; (لها) like «لهم», attached to (اجنح); (الواو) conjunction; (توكّل) like «اجنح»; (على الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (توكّل); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogating particle (nāsikh) —, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna; (هو) a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) [Note: Or a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ, whose khabar is «السميع», the nominal clause being the khabar of inna.]; (السميع) khabar of inna, nominative; (العليم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «جنحوا …» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «تنفقوا».
The clause «اجنح لها …» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «توكّل …» is in the position of the jussive, being conjoined to the apodosis of the condition.
The clause «إنّه هو السميع» has no grammatical position, giving the reason (taʿlīliyya).
(الواو) conjunction; (إن يريدوا) the conditional particle and the protasis, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (يخدعوا) imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn … and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of the condition; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogating particle —; (حسب) the noun of inna, accusative, and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الله) the Name of Majesty, khabar, nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يخدعوك) is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi.
(هو) a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as khabar; (أيّد) past verb, and the fāʿil is "huwa", and (الكاف) as before; (بنصر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أيّد), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (بالمؤمنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what the preceding preposition is attached to, for it is conjoined to it, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «يريدوا …» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «جنحوا».
The clause «يخدعوك …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «إنّ حسبك الله» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «هو الذي …» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption or giving the reason.
The clause «أيدك …» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
(الواو) conjunction; (ألّف) like «أيّد»; (بين) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (ألّف); (قلوب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle; (أنفقت) past verb and its fāʿil; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila of «ما»; (جميعا) ḥāl, accusative; (ما) particle of negation; (ألّفت) like «أنفقت»; (بين قلوبهم) like the first, attached to (ألّفت); (الواو) conjunction; (لكنّ) a particle of istidrāk (rectification) governing the accusative; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of lākinna, accusative; (ألّف) like «أيّد»; (بين) like the first, attached to (ألّف), and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إنّه عزيز حكيم) like «إنّ الله قويّ شديد» [Note: In verse (52) of this sūra.].
The clause «ألّف …» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «أيّدك».
The clause «أنفقت …» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «ما ألّفت …» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «لكنّ الله ألّف …» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause of the apodosis.
The clause «ألّف …» is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of lākinna.
The clause «إنّه عزيز …» has no grammatical position, having the status of giving the reason.

* Morphology:
(رباط): a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar of the triliteral verb ربط; it is not the maṣdar of the quadriliteral رابط, because here it means confinement (ḥabs) … Al-Zamakhsharī said: «الرباط» is a name for the horses that are tethered in the way of Allah; it may be that they are named by «الرباط» in the sense of «المرابطة» (garrisoning), and it may be the plural of ربيط in the sense of مربوط (tethered); and the maṣdar here is annexed to its object. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «الرباط» is a noun from رابط مرابطة, when one stays constantly at the enemy's frontier.
(يوفّ): it contains a weak-letter change by deletion (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf) suited to the jussive: the alif was dropped from it; its pattern is يقعّ. [Translator's note: so in the source; the dropped letter is the final yāʾ (يوفّى), and the pattern would be expected as يفعّ.]

* Rhetoric:
The non-metaphorical trope (al-majāz al-mursal): in the words of Allah the Exalted «وَأَعِدُّوا لَهُمْ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ مِنْ قُوَّةٍ» …
i.e. prepare against them what weapons you can, because they give strength, self-confidence and the ability to fight. So strength here is caused by the weapons, and the relation here is that of being caused (musabbabiyya).

* Benefits:
Artistic imagery in the Noble Qur'an:
In this verse occur the words of Allah the Exalted «وَإِنْ جَنَحُوا لِلسَّلْمِ فَاجْنَحْ لَها وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ». «السلم» is peace-making, which is something abstract, but the Quranic expression embodies it as though it were something tangible, by using the verb (جنح). On the other hand, the verb «جنح», by its sound, its meaning and what it creates in the imagination, depicts the sense of inclining and leaning towards reconciliation and peace. Here depiction and embodiment reach their utmost, and the imagination follows the image of peace and the inclining towards it as though it were present before one. If we tried to replace the verb «جنح» with another verb synonymous with it or close to it in meaning, that image would disappear and the movement and life in it would die. Herein lies the magic and inimitability of the speech of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: the choice of the word, the verb or the particle has come in a place that is its own, which cannot be exchanged or altered, as though the word had been placed by a balance and sent down into its appointed place.

safi-cedvel:12-13.t:
* I'rab:
(إذ) badal (substitute) of the first [Note: In verse (11) of this sūra; and it may be attached to (يثبّت).], (يوحي) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ; (ربّ) fāʿil (agent), nominative, and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إلى الملائكة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يوحي), (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb – an abrogator (nāsikh) – and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as ism of anna; (مع) an adverb, accusative (manṣūb), attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of anna, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّي معكم) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, i.e. بأنّي معكم ..., attached to (يوحي).
(الفاء) connecting an implied apodosis; (ثبّتوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (آمنوا) past verb and its fāʿil; (السين) a particle of the future; (ألقي) like يوحي, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «I» (أنا); (في قلوب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ألقي), (الذين) a relative in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (كفروا) like آمنوا; (الرعب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الفاء) conjunctive; (اضربوا) like ثبّتوا; (فوق) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to the verb اضربوا, and the object of اضربوا is omitted, its implied form being اضربوهم [Note: Some allowed (فوق) to be moved out of adverbial use and made an object by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa); Abū Ḥayyān rejected that.], (الأعناق) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunctive; (اضربوا) like ثبّتوا; (من) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of كلّ بنان; (كلّ) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (بنان) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «يوحيّ ربّك» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «ثبّتوا ...» is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if the fighting begins, then make firm ...
The clause «آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (الذين).
The clause «سألقي» has no grammatical position: an explanation of His saying أنّي معكم ... or a parenthesis between two conjoined clauses.
The clause «كفروا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «اضربوا ...» is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the clause ثبّتوا.
The clause «اضربوا (the second)» is conjoined to the clause اضربوا (the first).
(ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address; (الباء) a preposition of causation; (أن) a particle resembling the verb – an abrogator – and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the accusative as ism of anna; (شاقّوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (رسول) conjoined by the wāw to the Name of Majesty, accusative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّهم شاقّوا ...) is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ذلك.. i.e. that torment or punishment is because of their opposing Allah the Exalted and His Messenger. (الواو) resumptive; (من) a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (يشاقق) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), given a kasra because of the meeting of two sukūns, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being «he», referring to من; (الله) the Name of Majesty, like the previous, and likewise (رسوله), (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of the condition [Note: Or it is causal, for those who make the recompense omitted, the clause after it being a reason for this recompense, i.e.: whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger, He will punish him, for Allah is severe in punishment.], (إن) a particle resembling the verb – an abrogator –; (الله) the Name of Majesty, ism of inna, accusative; (شديد) khabar, nominative; (العقاب) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «ذلك بأنّهم ...» has no grammatical position: a reason for the content of the preceding torment.
The clause «شاقّوا ...» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of anna.
The clause «من يشاقق ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يشاقق ...» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.] The clause «إن الله شديد ...» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(الأعناق): plural of عنق, a noun for the well-known body part; its pattern is فعل with ḍamma on the fāʾ and ḍamma or sukūn on the ʿayn; it is masculine and feminine.
(بنان): a non-derived (jāmid) noun for the fingertips or the fingers; its pattern is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ; its singular is بنانة.

* Rhetoric:
Figurative usage (al-majāz): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَاضْرِبُوا مِنْهُمْ كُلَّ بَنانٍ», the speech is figurative in naming the whole by the name of the part. البنان is the finger; He expressed it by the part, which is the finger, and meant the whole, which is the hands and feet. So the relation is part-to-whole (juzʾiyya).

* Benefits:
- Among the characteristics of the Arabic language is making pronunciation easy; therefore the Arabs agreed on things that are all means to this end, among them «assimilation» (al-idghām), which is of three kinds:
a- Obligatory: when the two like letters are both vowelled, under conditions that may reach eleven, whose detail the method of this book does not allow, e.g. «مدّ», originally مدد, and ملّ and حبّ, etc.
b- Permissible: assimilation is permissible in three cases. (The first) if the verb is a past verb beginning with two tāʾs, like تتبّع and تتابع: assimilation is permissible in both, and pronouncing it is made possible by adding the connecting hamza, so one says اتّبع and اتّابع. (The second and third) that the word is a jussive imperfect verb, or an imperative verb indeclinable on the sukūn; in it both separation and assimilation are permissible, like the verb يشاقق in the verse referred to.
b- [Translator's note: so lettered in the source; «c» is meant.] Assimilation is prohibited if one of the two like letters, the first or the second, is vowelled [Translator's note: so in the source.], or if the first is a hāʾ of pause, or a long vowel at the end, or a separated hamza.

safi-cedvel:14-14.t:
* I'rab:
(ذلكم) like the preceding [Note: In the previous verse (13).], and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being «occurring» (واقع) or «deserved» (مستحقّ) [Note: (ذلك) may be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being «the matter» or «the punishment».], (الفاء) conjunctive [Note: According to Abū Ḥayyān, it is the answer of an implied command, i.e. take heed, then taste it.], (ذوقوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الواو) conjunctive; (أنّ) like the previous [Note: In the previous verse (13).]. (للكافرين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted, fronted khabar of أنّ; (عذاب) the postponed ism of anna, accusative (manṣūb); (النار) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr).
The clause «ذلكم (واقع)» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ذو قوه» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. take heed, then taste it..
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ للكافرين عذاب ...) is in the position of the nominative as khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being «the decreed thing» or «the necessary thing».. or in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, its implied form being «decreed», i.e. the fixedness of the torment of the Fire for the disbelievers is decreed [Note: It may be in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being اعلموا (know).].
The clause of the interpreted maṣdar – the mubtadaʾ and khabar – has no grammatical position: conjoined to the first resumptive clause.

* Rhetoric:
The shift (al-iltifāt): in the noble verse, since the address in it is to the disbelievers by way of a shift from the third person.

* Benefits:
1- «ذلكم»:
It is known to all grammarians that «ذا» is a demonstrative, that the lām is for distance, and that the kāf is a particle of address. What we want to clarify is that the demonstrative «ذلك» is always followed by a particle suited to the one addressed in singular, dual and plural, masculine and feminine. So you say: ذلك for the singular, ذلكما for the dual, ذلكم for the masculine plural and ذلكنّ for the feminine plural. In the discussion of the demonstrative there is detail and clarification that we have passed over, in keeping with our method in this book.

safi-cedvel:15-16.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) a vocative particle; (أيّ) the one addressed (munādā), a specific indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of the accusative, and (ها) for alerting (tanbīh); (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative as badal (substitute) of أيّ or its naʿt (adjective) [Translator's note: so in the source, «in the position of the accusative».]; (آمنوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (إذا) a conditional adverb for the future, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the content of the apodosis; (لقيتم) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn ... and (تم) a pronoun, fāʿil; (الذين) a relative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (كفروا) like آمنوا; (زحفا) a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of the ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object pronoun in (لقيتم), or of the subject pronoun, or of both together [Note: Or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted ḥāl, i.e. زاحفين زحفا (advancing in an advance).], (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of the condition; (لا) prohibitive, jussive-making; (تولّوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (هم) a pronoun, first mafʿūl bihi; (الأدبار) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb).
The vocative clause «يأيّها الذين ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لقيتم ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause of the condition, its verb and its apodosis has no grammatical position: answer to the vocative.
The clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the second relative noun (الذين).
The clause «لا تولّوهم ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
(الواو) conjunctive; (من يولّ) like من يشاقق, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يولّ) [Note: It may be indeclinable because it is annexed to an indeclinable adverb, namely (إذ).], (إذ) an adverbial noun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi [Note: The nunation here is the nunation of compensation (tanwīn ʿiwaḍ), compensating for an omitted clause, i.e. يوم إذ لقيتموهم (on the day when you meet them).], (دبر) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إلّا) a particle of exception; (متحرّفا) accusative as excepted from an implied general ḥāl [Note: I.e. whoever turns his back to them in whatever state, except turning aside ... If that is not implied, the entry of (إلّا) is not valid, because the condition is affirmative, not negated.. Some make (متحرّفا) excepted from those who turn their backs, i.e. whoever turns his back to them.. except a man turning aside; al-Zamakhsharī said this.], (لقتال) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the active participle متحرّف; (أو) a conjunction; (متحيّزا) conjoined to (متحرّفا), accusative; (إلى فئة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (متحيّزا), (الفاء) connecting the apodosis of the condition; (قد) a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (باء) past verb, and the fāʿil is «he»; (بغضب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil, i.e. clothed with or accompanied by wrath; (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt of غضب; (الواو) conjunctive; (مأوى) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (جهنّم) khabar (predicate), nominative, (الواو) conjunctive; (بئس) an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for the performative of blame; (المصير) fāʿil, nominative.. and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being جهنّم.
The clause «من يولّهم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause answering the vocative.
The clause «يولّهم ...» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.].
The clause «قد باء بغضب» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «مأواه جهنّم» is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «بئس المصير» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(زحفا): an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the triliteral verb زحف; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(تولّوا): it contains a weakening (iʿlāl) by deletion. Its origin is تولّيوا with ḍamma on the yāʾ; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was found heavy, so its vowel was moved to the letter before it; when two sukūns met, the yāʾ, the final radical of the word, was deleted and it became تولّوا; its pattern is تفعّوا.
(يولّهم): it contains a weakening by deletion in keeping with the jussive; its origin is يولّيهم; its pattern is يفعّهم.
(متحرّفا): the active participle of the five-letter تحرّف, so its pattern is متفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(متحيّزا): the active participle of the five-letter تحيّز, so its pattern is متفعّل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn. It contains a weakening, because its origin is متحيوز: the yāʾ and the wāw met, the first of them quiescent, so the wāw was changed into a yāʾ and assimilated into the first yāʾ.
(باء): it contains a weakening by change, since the alif is originally a wāw – its imperfect is يبوء – and its origin is بوأ. The wāw came vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was changed into «the fāʾ» [Translator's note: so in the source; «into an alif» is evidently meant.].

* Rhetoric:
The figure of allusion (fann al-taʿrīḍ): in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وَمَنْ يُوَلِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ دُبُرَهُ». He mentioned to them a state that is deemed shameful in the one who does it, so He used the word الدبر (the rear) rather than الظهر (the back). Some include it within metonymy (al-kināya).
al-Saʿd al-Taftāzānī said: «When the metonymy is incidental, brought for the sake of a qualified thing that is not mentioned, it is fitting to call it allusion (al-taʿrīḍ). One says عرضت لفلان and عرضت بفلان when you say something while meaning him, as though you pointed to one side while intending another side; and from it are the indirect expressions (al-maʿārīḍ) in speech, which is the concealment (al-tawriya) of a thing by another thing.
